input.quote: Thereafter, this Agreement shall automatically renew for subsequent one (1) year periods unless either party provides the other party with written notification at least thirty (30) days prior to the expiration of the initial five (5) year term or any one (1) year renewal thereof of its intention to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale: Section 11.1 already meets the preferred mechanics on renewal length (12-month renewals) and exit (either party may opt out on 30 days' written notice), so no change is needed there. However, the clause omits two elements of our position: a Commerce One reminder 60 days before renewal, and any cap on renewal pricing. Exhibit B prices only "Year 2-5, and beyond" with no uplift limit, leaving renewal fees uncapped for Corio as the paying licensee. We added a 60-day renewal reminder and a renewal uplift cap of the lesser of CPI and 3%, with a 5% fallback offered.

proposal.summary: Add renewal reminder and cap renewal fee increases at lesser of CPI and 3%
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We kept the 12-month renewal terms and 30-day opt-out, but added a 60-day renewal reminder from Commerce One and capped any renewal fee increase at the lesser of CPI and 3%, consistent with our position that renewals be predictably priced and easy to exit. If 3% is unworkable, we can accept a 5% cap as a fallback.

ops.newText: of its intention to terminate this Agreement. Commerce One shall provide Corio with a written reminder of the upcoming automatic renewal at least sixty (60) days prior to the expiration of the then-current term. The fees payable for any one (1) year renewal period shall not increase by more than the lesser of (i) the percentage increase in the U.S. Consumer Price Index (All Urban Consumers) over the preceding twelve (12) months and (ii) three percent (3%) of the fees payable for the immediately preceding period.
